# Video AI section (Modules VD01-VD15, Labs 1-8)
#
# CPU-only and installable on top of cpu.txt. The section's own videos and
# annotations are generated by scripts/make_video_data.py, so nothing here
# downloads data. Only Lab 2 / Lab 4 need network access, and only on the first
# run: they fetch the COCO-pretrained SSDLite320 weights through torchvision
# (13 MB) into projects/video-ai/.cache/torch via TORCH_HOME. Both labs degrade
# to a reported "pretrained detector unavailable" path when the download cannot
# happen, so the rest of the section is fully offline.
#
# Why OpenCV is required here (unlike the computer vision section):
#   * every lab decodes and encodes video, and OpenCV is the only video I/O the
#     course depends on. The headless wheel is used on purpose: no GUI, no
#     display server, no Qt dependency.
#   * the writers verified for this section are mp4v (MP4), MJPG and XVID (AVI).
#     H.264/avc1 needs the OpenH264 library, which the wheel does not bundle, and
#     video.VideoWriter reports that as a clear VideoError instead of writing an
#     empty file.
#
# Why not ffmpeg, decord, av, or moviepy:
#   * each adds a native binary or a second decoding API for students to learn,
#     and none is needed for the operations in these labs (sequential decode,
#     stride sampling, single-frame access, write).
#   * SciPy is used for the Hungarian assignment in the tracker, which would
#     otherwise need scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment reimplemented.
#
# Verified on Windows 11 / Python 3.12.10 / CPU with:
#   opencv-python-headless 4.14.0, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1,
#   torch 2.14.1+cpu, torchvision 0.29.1+cpu
#
# Note: opencv-python and opencv-python-headless must not both be installed; the
# headless wheel wins or conflicts depending on install order. Uninstall the GUI
# wheel first if you have it.

torch>=2.2,<3
torchvision>=0.17,<1
opencv-python-headless>=4.8,<5
numpy>=1.26,<3
scipy>=1.11,<2

# Optional: only for the notebook in notebooks/video-ai, which imports the same
# video_core modules the labs use. The labs themselves never need Jupyter.
#   jupyterlab (see requirements/notebooks.txt)
